message.content: {"research_brief": "How can I reconstruct, using only evidence returned by the benchmark tools and citing exclusively the source IDs those tools provide, the complete public evidence chain for the 2023 3CX DesktopApp software supply-chain compromise—specifically: (1) how the compromise was initially initiated, including the earliest publicly evidenced access, payload, or prerequisite activity; (2) how the malicious activity propagated into or affected 3CX’s build environment and software-development/release process; (3) how the compromised DesktopApp reached users and what publicly evidenced artifacts, stages, or mechanisms connected the initial intrusion to the distributed application; and (4) which threat-activity cluster the incident was publicly attributed to, clearly distinguishing confirmed facts from vendor, government, researcher, or media assessments, allegations, competing attributions, and unresolved uncertainty? I should produce a complete, readable Markdown final report without asking whether to continue, avoid inventing or inferring unsupported facts, use only tool-returned evidence and source IDs, identify contradictions or attribution uncertainty, and include a fenced JSON object with exactly the arrays `findings`, `claims`, `reasoning_steps`, and `contradictions`: each finding must contain `question`, `answer`, `supporting_entities`, and `source_references`; each claim must contain `claim` and `source_references`; each reasoning step must contain `id`, `conclusion`, `premise_entities`, and `premise_relations`; and each contradiction must contain `contradiction_id`, `description`, and `source_references`. I should use entity IDs and relationship names only when they are explicitly supported by benchmark-tool evidence, label all allegations, assessments, and uncertainty, and omit any unsupported detail."}
